page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-2 is an Arm-based general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory. Built upon the arm64 architecture, this instance maintains a standard memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, aligning with common general-purpose operational profiles. It does not include integrated hardware accelerators, providing zero GPUs, and relies entirely on external network-attached volumes as it lacks local storage.

With dedicated CPU core allocation, the instance delivers consistent processor availability without resource contention or burstable throttling mechanisms. Because local persistent storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not bundled with this configuration, external storage options and network routing must be provisioned independently. From an operational efficiency perspective, the Arm-based architecture provides resource-dense compute capacity with standard memory allocation for entry-level deployments.

The c4a-standard-2 is suited for moderate general-purpose workloads that are compatible with arm64 architectures. Typical deployments include microservices, lightweight web servers, containerized application environments, background task workers, and developmental test environments that do not require intense local I/O or specialized hardware acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine utilizing the arm64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance configuration operates with dedicated CPU execution, eliminating the variable throttling associated with shared-core tiers. Local storage is absent, meaning storage capacity must be provisioned via remote block storage, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators are included. The combination of dedicated Arm compute resources and balanced memory allocation makes this instance a practical option for standard multi-tier enterprise workloads, API backends, lightweight web serving, and containerized microservices compiled for 64-bit Arm environments.
